close_reason: Decision ratified — defense already committed to source in digest.rs:143-158 (type-level rustdoc on Sha256 explains the #[serde(try_from = "String")] adapter routes every deserialize path through Sha256::from_hex, keeping the ABNF validator as single source of truth) and reinforced by digest.rs:301-306 (rustdoc on TryFrom<String> impl explaining the move-not-clone path the adapter takes). The decision-record-grade rationale is committed and pinned. Pattern mirrors how sibling DEFEND-ON-REVIEW beads .7 and .8 were closed (commit c430f73).
description: DEFEND ON REVIEW: digest.rs:99-102 derives Serialize/Deserialize with #[serde(try_from = "String", into = "String")]. This routes every deserialize path (serde_json::from_str, from_value, from_reader) through TryFrom<String>, which calls Sha256::from_hex, which applies the ABNF validator. A future contributor might suggest writing a hand-rolled impl Deserialize for Sha256 to (a) emit a more JMAP-specific error message, or (b) reject the input earlier (visit_str without allocating). Resist both: (a) the current error already names the byte position via Display, and (b) the visit_str variant would need to re-implement the same validator logic and would skew over time from from_hex. The adapter pattern keeps validation in one place — from_hex — which is the single source of truth tested in 11 of the 19 unit tests. Keep this decision.
title: Sha256 #[serde(try_from, into)] adapter routes Deserialize through TryFrom — defend over a custom Deserialize impl
